messages:
ade: short heads-up: we keep undercounting model-edge costs when a single request fans out to multiple GPUs/models (split-embed -> rerank -> generator). current signals only record the final generator model and omit earlier encoder/embedding token usage. this skews per-model cost dashboards and makes optrank alerts noisy.

sam: yeah, saw that in the invoices for tenant-42 last month. any practical proposals?

ade: proposal: a compact per-request billing envelope emitted at the edge containing a list of model calls (id shorthand), role (embed|score|gen), input_tokens, output_tokens, and an origin tag (edge/proxy/runtime). keep it line-oriented and tiny. runtime emits on each outgoing model RPC and the edge aggregates before responding (so we have canonical order). example payload: 

```
X-RW-BILL: rid=abc123; calls=3; c0=mid:emd-sm,role:embed,itoks:32,otoks:0; c1=mid:rrk-lg,role:score,itoks:8,otoks:4; c2=mid:gen-xl,role:gen,itoks:16,otoks:120; origin=edge
```

viv: nice. two follow-ups: 1) what if proxies re-request a model (retry) or we replay from cache? 2) how do we avoid exploding cardinality by attaching model_version to every metric?

ade: for retries we include a retry_count per call and a cache_flag. billing job will dedupe using (rid, call_index) plus retry_count. for cardinality: don't index model full_version in the live TSDB; store only model_family tag (e.g., gen-xl). write the full model_version -> owner mapping to a separate low-throughput table used by billing offline jobs.

sam: sampling strategy? high-traffic tenants will still flood us with envelopes.

ade: keep 100% compact envelopes (single-line header) but sample the verbose JSON envelopes (where we attach raw token breakouts and prompt hashes). deterministic sampling by hash(rid) so audits are reproducible. sample rate is tenant-configurable and must be logged in billing jobs.

obs-bot: infra-note: created ticket OBS-7811 to add X-RW-BILL header to runtime, preserve through proxies, and add sampled_verbose flag.

billing-bot: FYI billing pipeline will need a new ingestion step to expand compact envelopes into per-model charge rows. will propose a schema for nightly job.

viv: edge-case: multi-tenant shared routing pool where a single GPU batch contains requests from different tenants and models. how do we attribute per-GPU kernel time vs per-request token cost?

ade: we separate two concerns: token-based unit costs (tracked via envelope) and infra-level kernel time (tracked via GPU telemetry annotated with batch composition). nightly job will join batch records to envelopes using batch_id + rid set to apportion GPU seconds. we must ensure batch_id propagation is present in runtime logs.

sam: operational risk: if edge fails to attach envelope we lose attribution. should runtime synthesize?

ade: yes, synthesize at first-hop with origin=runtime and mark synthetic=true. ingest will surface a hit-rate metric for synthetic envelopes so we can iterate.

viv: concrete next steps: 1) final header ABNF and max-bytes limit (ade), 2) runtime + proxy PRs to emit and passthrough headers (sam), 3) ingest change to persist compact envelopes to cold-store and verbose sampled to hot-store (infra), 4) billing job design doc for join logic with GPU batch telemetry (billing). I'll volunteer to write the billing doc.

ade: I'll draft the header ABNF and an RFC with cost/ingest estimates by Friday. ping me for review. :memo:
